subject: math
cluster: Work with radicals and integer exponents
intro: Estimate large numbers by rounding to a single nonzero digit and writing them as a single digit times an integer power of 10. The exponent counts how many places the decimal point moves. Then practice reading off which power-of-10 number is larger and by how many powers of 10.

items.prompt: Write $3{,}000{,}000$ as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: Count the places the decimal point moves from $3{,}000{,}000.$ to $3.$: it moves $6$ places to the left.

items.prompt: Write $50{,}000$ as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: Move the decimal point from $50{,}000.$ to $5.$: that is $4$ places left.

items.prompt: Round $7{,}900{,}000{,}000$ to one nonzero digit, then write it as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The leading digit is $7$ and the next digit is $9$, which is $\ge 5$, so round up to $8$.
The decimal point moves $9$ places from $8{,}000{,}000{,}000.$ to $8.$

items.prompt: Round $4{,}200{,}000$ to one nonzero digit, then write it as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The leading digit is $4$ and the next digit is $2$, which is $<5$, so round down (keep $4$).
The decimal point moves $6$ places, so $4{,}200{,}000 \approx 4 \times 10^{6}$.

items.prompt: Round $610{,}000$ to one nonzero digit, then write it as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The leading digit is $6$ and the next digit is $1$, which is $<5$, so keep $6$.
The decimal point moves $5$ places, so $610{,}000 \approx 6 \times 10^{5}$.
An exponent of $5$ means move the decimal point $5$ places to the right.
An exponent of $3$ means move the decimal point $3$ places to the right.

items.prompt: Which is larger, $1 \times 10^{4}$ or $1 \times 10^{7}$? By how many powers of 10?
items.answer: $1 \times 10^{7}$ is larger, by $3$ powers of 10 (about $1{,}000$ times as large).

steps: Both numbers have the same leading digit $1$, so compare the exponents.
The exponent is $7 - 4 = 3$ greater, so it is about $10^{3} = 1{,}000$ times as large.

items.prompt: Which is larger, $1 \times 10^{6}$ or $1 \times 10^{5}$? By how many powers of 10?
items.answer: $1 \times 10^{6}$ is larger, by $1$ power of 10 (about $10$ times as large).

steps: Both numbers have the same leading digit $1$, so compare the exponents.
The exponent is $6 - 5 = 1$ greater, so it is about $10^{1} = 10$ times as large.

items.prompt: About how many times as large is $1 \times 10^{8}$ as $1 \times 10^{5}$?

steps: So the result is $1 \times 10^{3} = 1{,}000$ times as large.

items.prompt: Write $80{,}000{,}000$ as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The decimal point moves $7$ places from $80{,}000{,}000.$ to $8.$

items.prompt: Round $3{,}100{,}000{,}000$ to one nonzero digit, then write it as a single digit times an integer power of 10.

steps: The leading digit is $3$ and the next digit is $1$, which is $<5$, so keep $3$.
The decimal point moves $9$ places, so $3{,}100{,}000{,}000 \approx 3 \times 10^{9}$.
An exponent of $8$ means move the decimal point $8$ places to the right.

items.prompt: Which is larger, $4 \times 10^{5}$ or $4 \times 10^{8}$? By how many powers of 10?
items.answer: $4 \times 10^{8}$ is larger, by $3$ powers of 10 (about $1{,}000$ times as large).

steps: Both numbers have the same leading digit $4$, so compare the exponents.
The exponent is $8 - 5 = 3$ greater, so it is about $10^{3} = 1{,}000$ times as large.

items.prompt: About how many times as large is $1 \times 10^{9}$ as $1 \times 10^{6}$?

steps: So the result is $1 \times 10^{3} = 1{,}000$ times as large.
